This uses your retail orders database after you added the `channels` table
with the [sales channels scripts](../lectures/retail-orders-channels-scripts.html).

This time [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com) writes the SQL. Copy each block
(use the copy button in its top right corner) and paste it into Gemini. Run
the blocks in order in the same chat: the table schemas tell Gemini what your
tables look like, so they have to go first.

Then copy the query Gemini writes into the DoltHub SQL editor for your retail
orders database and run it. Look at the result and check that it really
answers the question.

## Table Schemas to Give to AI

Paste this first to Gemini as you ask it to write queries for you. It shows
the four tables, their columns, and how they connect.

```sql
CREATE TABLE customers (
  customer_id int NOT NULL,
  first_name varchar(255),
  last_name varchar(255),
  email varchar(255),
  PRIMARY KEY (customer_id)
);

CREATE TABLE products (
  product_id int NOT NULL,
  name varchar(255),
  price decimal(10,2),
  description varchar(1023),
  PRIMARY KEY (product_id)
);

-- channel_name is one of: physical (in a store), ecom (the website),
-- mcom (a phone), scom (social media), pop-up (a temporary pop-up shop).
CREATE TABLE channels (
  channel_id int NOT NULL,
  channel_name varchar(50),
  description varchar(255),
  PRIMARY KEY (channel_id)
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id int NOT NULL,
  customer_id int NOT NULL,
  product_id int NOT NULL,
  order_date datetime,
  channel_id int,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (customer_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products (product_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (channel_id) REFERENCES channels (channel_id)
);
```

## 1. Where Each Order Came From

```default
For every order, show the order_id, the customer's first_name, the product's name, and the channel_name, sorted by order_id.
```

## 2. Orders and Revenue by Channel

```default
For each channel, show the channel_name, num_orders, the number of orders through that channel, and revenue, the total price of those orders, sorted from highest revenue to lowest.
```

## 3. Our Omnichannel Customers

```default
Show the first_name, last_name, and num_channels of every customer who bought through more than one channel.
```

## 4. Online vs. In Person

```default
Group the orders into online (ecom, mcom, scom) and in person (physical, pop-up), and show where_bought, num_orders, and revenue for each group.
```

## 5. Average Order Value by Channel

```default
For each channel, show the channel_name and avg_order_value, the average price of the orders through that channel, sorted from highest avg_order_value to lowest.
```

## 6. Channel Share of Revenue

```default
For each channel, show the channel_name and pct_of_revenue, that channel's share of the total revenue from all orders as a percent, sorted from highest to lowest.
```

## 7. Customer Reach by Channel

```default
For each channel, show the channel_name and num_customers, the number of different customers who ordered through it.
```

## 8. Products That Sell Everywhere

```default
Show the name and num_channels of every product that was sold through more than one channel.
```

## 9. Digital-Only Shoppers

```default
Show the first_name and last_name of every customer who has ordered online but never in person.
```
